subject: Termination notice lifecycle coordination and MSA checkpoints
messages:
From: Jane Lee <jane.lee@acme.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com; procurement@acme.com
Cc: Acme Legal <legal@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Question on notice windows and TFC for MSA + Order Form

Karthik,

Thanks for sending over the latest MSA and order form redlines. Our procurement team wants to lock down two items before we move to signature:

1) The auto-renewal trigger and how notice windows are calculated (calendar days vs. business days).
2) The scope and notice requirements for Termination for Convenience (TFC) — specifically whether a 60-day notice is sufficient if we also need an orderly transition period.

Can you confirm Redwood's standard position and whether you can accept Acme's request to change notice windows to 45 business days for large enterprise deals? We understand there may be operational impacts and would appreciate any compromise language you can propose.

Attached our internal procurement checklist for context.

Thanks,
Jane Lee
Head of Procurement — Acme Corporation
Attachment: procurement-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Jane Lee <jane.lee@acme.com>, procurement@acme.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 12:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on notice windows and TFC for MSA + Order Form

Hi Jane — thanks for the clear ask and the checklist. High level: we try to keep a predictable termination cadence while also making sure customers have time to transfer data/traffic. A few points and a pragmatic proposal below.

- Auto-renewal: Our baseline is calendar days with a 60-day notice prior to renewal. This aligns scheduling and billing cycles across customers.
- TFC: Standard 60-day notice in the MSA; we typically include a 90-day transition assistance window in the order form for customers that need migration support (this can be commercialized).

Compromise proposal we can sign off on for enterprise deals:
- Order form: 45 business days (explicit definition) for opt-out of auto-renewal if the customer commits to a 90-day transition assistance addendum (order-form SOW).
- MSA: Keep legal text at 60 calendar days for general applicability; add an order-form-specific exception clause pointing to the transition addendum.

I've attached MSA_redline_v3.docx showing the exact redline language (see section 6.2 for termination mechanics and section 2.1 for term/renewal). If that looks reasonable to Acme we can route to Legal for a narrow variance approval.

Next steps: Laura, Hannah — can you confirm if legal is comfortable with a 45 business-day carve-out being implemented via order form + transition addendum (so MSA stays standard)? If yes, I'll propose the language to Jane and move to DocuSign.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
Attachment: MSA_redline_v3.docx (redline stub)

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Question on notice windows and TFC for MSA + Order Form

Karthik — thanks for the draft approach. Quick thoughts from Legal:

- We prefer to keep the master MSA language consistent across customers to avoid precedent risk.
- Implementing the 45 business-day opt-out solely in the order form + a clearly scoped transition addendum is acceptable, provided the order form references the MSA section and the addendum limits Redwood's obligations to defined activities (e.g., data export, runbook delivery, limited stubbed support).
- We need to avoid open-ended transition assistance obligations; recommend a hard cap (90 days or X hours of engineering) and a defined out clause if extra work is required.

Hannah — please confirm operational feasibility of a 90-day transition assistance package and whether we should price it as a standalone SKU or roll into the order form for this deal.

If everyone agrees, I can prepare a short legal approval memo and the exact addendum language for the order form.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Jane Lee <jane.lee@acme.com>, procurement@acme.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 14:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on notice windows and TFC for MSA + Order Form

Jane — looping back with an agreed pathway. Summary of what Redwood can accept for Acme Corp (so we can finalize the order form):

1) Auto-renewal opt-out: 45 business days (we'll define business days in the order form as Mon–Fri excluding Redwood-observed US federal holidays). This will be captured in the Order Form as a specific paragraph that overrides the MSA renewal notice for this deal only.

2) TFC + Transition Assistance: MSA will retain a 60-calendar-day TFC baseline. Order form will include a Transition Addendum that provides up to 90 days of transition assistance (deliverables: data export, KV cache dump, runbook handoff, two 4-hour on-call windows for cutover). Any additional engineering beyond the 90 days will be subject to a statement-of-work and time-and-materials.

3) Pricing/sku: Hannah — our Ops/PM recommendation is to price the 90-day transition assistance as a fixed, one-time SKU for this enterprise deal. If we bundle, we should make the addendum non-refundable and clearly scoped.

If both Laura and Hannah confirm, I'll update the redline and send a DocuSign packet with the order form + transition addendum for signature. Jane — if this is acceptable, please confirm and I’ll get the packet over today.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
